meta.purpose: Deterministic guidance for youths in the first 10 minutes after online harm. The engine decides the route from a fixed rule table; no AI judgement.
meta.framework: Maps to IMDA 'Report Inappropriate Content' + 'Engage & Support' and the Add / Check / Tell framework.
meta.links_checked: Official Singapore links verified Nov 2026: osc.gov.sg, police.gov.sg, scamshield.gov.sg, she.org.sg. Re-confirm before relying on them.

options.label: Someone shared or threatened to share intimate photos of me
Someone is pretending to be me
I was scammed or someone is trying to scam me

questions.title: Is this happening right now, or are you in danger?

options.label: Yes, right now / I feel unsafe

instagram.label: Instagram
instagram.report: Open the post, profile or message, tap the ••• menu, choose Report, and pick the reason (nudity, harassment, or pretending to be someone).

tiktok.label: TikTok
tiktok.report: Press and hold the video or message, or tap Share then Report, and follow the steps.

telegram.label: Telegram
telegram.report: Open the chat or channel, tap the name at the top, choose Report, and select the reason.

whatsapp.label: WhatsApp
whatsapp.report: Open the chat, tap the contact name, scroll down and tap Report (this reports and blocks together).

discord.label: Discord
discord.report: Tap and hold the message, choose Report, and keep the message link if you can.

other.label: this platform
other.report: Find the app or site's Report or Safety option (often under the ••• menu or Settings) and report the content.

support.label: You deserve support. These are free and confidential:
lines: Samaritans of Singapore (SOS): call 1767 or text 9151 1767, 24 hours
mindline.sg — free mental health support: https://mindline.sg

intimate_images.label: Intimate images shared or threatened
intimate_images.headline: Let's protect you first. You are not in trouble.
add: Do NOT delete anything yet. The messages and posts are your evidence.
Screenshot the message or post so it shows the username, the date, and the link (URL).
Do NOT forward the image itself to anyone, not even to show proof.
Do NOT reply to threats or pay anything if someone is demanding money.
Block the person ONLY AFTER you have taken your screenshots.
check: Report it on the platform where it happened (steps below).
Report directly to the Online Safety Commission (OSC) to get it taken down — intimate-image abuse can be reported straight away, free: https://www.osc.gov.sg
For specialised help (counselling, free legal clinic, fast takedowns), contact SHECARES@SCWO: call 8001 01 4616 or WhatsApp 8985 5528 (Mon–Fri 9am–9pm) — https://she.org.sg
tell: Talk to someone you trust today. You should not carry this alone.

doxxing.label: Personal information posted (doxxing)
doxxing.headline: Let's secure your info and get it taken down.
add: Do NOT delete anything yet. Keep the posts as evidence.
Screenshot the post showing the username, the date, and the link (URL).
Write down where your info appears (which app, which account).
Make your accounts private and turn on two-factor login if you can.
Block the person AFTER you have screenshots.
check: Report the post on the platform (steps below) and ask for it to be removed.
Report directly to the Online Safety Commission (OSC) — doxxing can be reported straight away, free: https://www.osc.gov.sg
Posting someone's private info to harass them may be an offence under the Protection from Harassment Act.
tell: Tell someone you trust so you are not handling this on your own.

harassment.label: Harassment or bullying
harassment.headline: This isn't your fault. Let's slow it down and get help.
add: Do NOT delete the messages. They show what is happening.
Screenshot the messages or comments with the username, date, and link (URL).
Mute or limit comments if the app allows it, to lower the pressure right now.
Block the person AFTER you have taken screenshots.
check: Report the account or messages on the platform first (steps below).
If it doesn't stop, you can escalate to the Online Safety Commission (OSC) 24 hours after reporting it to the platform, free: https://www.osc.gov.sg
Ongoing harassment may be covered by the Protection from Harassment Act.
tell: Tell someone you trust. Being believed makes a real difference.

impersonation.label: Someone impersonating you
impersonation.headline: Let's prove it's you and shut the fake account down.
add: Do NOT delete anything. Keep links to the fake account.
Screenshot the fake profile showing its username, the date, and the link (URL).
Tell close friends not to interact with the fake account for now.
Secure your real account: change your password and turn on two-factor login.
check: Use the platform's impersonation report to say this account is pretending to be you (steps below). You may be asked for proof of identity.
If the fake account stays up, report it to the Online Safety Commission (OSC), free: https://www.osc.gov.sg
tell: Let someone you trust know, so they can help and watch for the fake account.

scam.label: Scam
scam.headline: Let's stop the money and report it. This happens to lots of people.
add: Do NOT send any more money, and stop replying to the person.
Screenshot the chats, the account/number, and any transfer details.
If you shared a password or OTP, change that password now and tell your bank.
Don't delete the conversation — it's evidence.
check: Report and check suspicious numbers, links or messages with ScamShield — call the 24/7 helpline 1799 or use the app: https://www.scamshield.gov.sg
If you lost money or gave away sensitive details, make a Police report (not just a ScamShield report): https://www.police.gov.sg/e-services/lodge-police-report
You can report the scam account on the platform too (steps below).
tell: Tell someone you trust — scams rely on you feeling too embarrassed to speak up.

danger_now_yes.banner_text: If you are in immediate danger, or someone is threatening you (e.g. 'pay or I post your photos'), call the Police at 999 now.
danger_now_yes.add_first: If you are in immediate danger, call Police 999 first.
danger_now_yes.check_add: Because this is happening now, call the Police at 999 for emergencies, or make a non-emergency report online: https://www.police.gov.sg/e-services/lodge-police-report

danger_now_no.banner_text: You have time. Let's do this step by step.
danger_now_no.check_add: If you ever feel unsafe, you can call 999, or make a non-emergency Police report online: https://www.police.gov.sg/e-services/lodge-police-report

under18_yes.tell_first: You're under 18, so telling a trusted adult now is the most important step: a parent, relative, teacher, school counsellor, or coach.

under18_no.tell_first: Tell someone you trust: a friend, family member, or counsellor. You don't have to handle this alone.

trusted_adult_message: Hi, something happened to me online and I need help. Can we talk when you have a moment? I haven't deleted anything and I'm following the steps to report it.
